screening_decisions.reason: The study discusses the FIGO staging system for endometrial carcinoma; it is not a randomized controlled trial and does not compare chemotherapy interventions.
RCT comparing doxorubicin alone vs. doxorubicin plus cyclophosphamide in advanced/recurrent endometrial carcinoma. Meets all selection criteria.

Phase III RCT comparing doxorubicin + cisplatin vs. doxorubicin + paclitaxel + filgrastim. Although the abstract does not explicitly state 'advanced', it is a GOG chemotherapy trial for endometrial cancer, and conservative inclusion is appropriate.
The study provides recommendations for reporting cancer treatment results; it is not a trial of chemotherapy in endometrial cancer.
This is a retrospective case series of pelvic exenteration for recurrent endometrial cancer, not an RCT.
RCT comparing adriamycin vs. cyclophosphamide in advanced endometrial cancer. Randomization and comparison of two chemotherapy agents.
Randomized phase II study comparing cisplatin alone vs. cyclophosphamide-doxorubicin-cisplatin in progestin-refractory advanced endometrial carcinoma. It is an RCT albeit phase II.
Randomised phase II study comparing cyclophosphamide vs. ifosfamide in advanced/recurrent endometrial carcinoma. RCT design.
Overview of beta-blocker trials after myocardial infarction; entirely unrelated to endometrial cancer or chemotherapy.

RCT comparing two multidrug regimens (melphalan/5-FU/megace vs. adriamycin/5-FU/cyclophosphamide/megace) in advanced/recurrent endometrial cancer. A small non-randomized subset does not invalidate the overall RCT design.
Methodological paper on extracting summary statistics for meta-analyses; not a clinical trial.
Phase III RCT comparing MVAC vs. AC in advanced primary or recurrent metastatic endometrial carcinoma. Meets criteria.
Phase III RCT of doxorubicin plus cisplatin with or without paclitaxel in advanced endometrial carcinoma. Meets criteria.
RCT of MIC chemotherapy in unresectable non-small cell lung cancer; wrong cancer type.
The abstract does not mention randomization; it appears to be a non-randomized comparison of three chemotherapy regimens. Does not meet the RCT requirement.
Methodological paper on incorporating time-to-event data into meta-analysis; not a trial.
This is a citation for a commentary/review on changes in endometrial cancer treatment; not an original study, let alone an RCT.
This is a Cochrane review protocol about adjuvant chemotherapy after hysterectomy. It is not an RCT, and the setting is adjuvant, which is excluded.
Cochrane systematic review on hormonal therapy for advanced/recurrent endometrial cancer; not a chemotherapy RCT.
This appears to be a narrative review or guideline on endometrial cancer surgery; not an RCT.
Retrospective analysis of treatment failure in endometrial carcinoma; not an RCT.

Phase III RCT comparing standard-timed vs. circadian-timed doxorubicin + cisplatin in stage III/IV or recurrent endometrial carcinoma. Compares chemotherapy scheduling, which falls under 'chemotherapy versus another intervention'.
Phase III RCT of doxorubicin with or without cisplatin in advanced endometrial carcinoma. Meets criteria.
RCT comparing doxorubicin alone vs. doxorubicin + cisplatin in advanced/recurrent endometrial adenocarcinoma. Meets criteria.
